summary: John's 3rd-great-grandfather; Plymouth laborer whose wife Catherine Scott divorced him; the census-proven link between Addison Pringle and the Croup/Lamoreaux lines (and so the SAR route).
bio: Andrew G. Pringle was born about 1836, probably in Plymouth Twp: he was 14 in the 1850 census (enumerated 14 Sep 1850) and 44 on 4 Jun 1880. The tree shows him as 1835-1900 (transcription: c1836-1900). The 1850 census of Plymouth Twp (A. Atherton, Ass't Marshal, page 140/141, stamp 71; dwelling 944/family 964) lists James Pringle 51 farmer ($500 real estate, b. PA), Elizabeth 48, Alby 27, Noah 16 farmer, Andrew 14 (line 38), Leva Ann 11 and Edwin 9. Two households earlier (dwelling 942) was the widow Hulda Pringle with children Orange, Ransom and 'Caturah'. The census states no relationships, but Noah is documented as son of James and Elizabeth (Croup) Pringle and grandson of Samuel and Martha (Lamoreaux), so Andrew's parentage is settled; John found this page himself on FamilySearch, attached to Andrew Pringle 1836-1900 (KG4S-XMF). He married Catherine Scott of Kingston in 1857; they had seven children per Bradsby. She later sued for divorce, 'the action commenced by her and sustained by the court'; no grounds are stated anywhere online. In the 1880 census (Plymouth Twp, ED 145, p.4) he was a laborer, with Katharine 43, John 20, Samuel 17, 'Adason' 15 (laborer), Orange 13 (slate picker) and Stella 5; next door was a 15-year-old servant, Emma Pringle, a relative of unknown connection. He named sons Orange and Samuel, following the Lamoreaux/Pringle naming pattern. He died in 1900 (tree; no record found). No Civil War, GAR, pension, will (not in the Luzerne wills index 'P') or occupation record was found online; he is not in the 2,656 Bates-transcribed PA company rosters on PA-Roots.
